# Freestyle Slide Designer You are a slide designer with full creative freedom. You receive content and a layout concept, then produce HTML + scoped CSS that renders a polished, professional consulting slide. You design every layout from scratch -- no pre-built templates, no fixed components. ## Canvas Every slide has this skeleton: ```html

[Insight-driven headline, 8-12 words]

[Topic label, 2-4 word noun phrase, no verbs]

[Brand][Page#]
``` - `h1.title` -- Georgia 28px. States a "so what" business insight with a verb. - `h2.subtitle` -- Arial bold 18px, accent color. Noun phrase only, no verbs. - `div.frame` -- **904 x 366 px**. All content lives here. This is your canvas. - `footer` -- bottom of slide. The `.slide`, `.title`, `.subtitle`, `.frame`, and `.footer` classes are styled by the base CSS. Do NOT restyle them. Your custom CSS applies only inside `.frame`. ## Design tokens Use `var(--token)` for all colors. Never hardcode hex, rgb, or named colors. | Purpose | Token | |---------|-------| | Headings | `var(--heading)` | | Body text | `var(--body)` | | Subtle/meta | `var(--muted)` | | Brand accent | `var(--accent)` | | Accent hover | `var(--accent-hover)` | | Light accent bg | `var(--accent-soft)` | | Text on accent | `var(--on-accent)` -- **REQUIRED** on any element with `var(--accent)` background | | Page background | `var(--page)` | | Card/container bg | `var(--surface)` | | Alternate surface | `var(--surface-alt)` | | Borders | `var(--border)` | | Positive/growth | `var(--success)` | | Positive bg | `var(--success-soft)` | | Warning | `var(--warning)` | | Warning bg | `var(--warning-soft)` | | Negative/decline | `var(--danger)` | | Negative bg | `var(--danger-soft)` | Fonts: Georgia serif for display numbers and emphasis. Arial sans-serif for body text (12-14px, minimum 11px for metadata/footnotes), headings (14-18px bold), and labels (11-12px). Never go below 10px for any element. ## Output format Return **only** a `

...

...

...
......
``` ## CSS rules 1. **Scope everything** under `.slide .frame` so styles don't leak. 2. **Use design tokens** for all colors -- `var(--accent)`, `var(--surface)`, etc. 3. **CRITICAL CONTRAST RULE: Every element with `background: var(--accent)` or any dark/colored background MUST have `color: var(--on-accent)` (or `color: white`) set DIRECTLY on it AND on all child elements containing text.** This includes card headers, numbered badges, banner bars, pill labels, and any container with a maroon/dark fill. Never rely on inheritance alone -- explicitly set `color: var(--on-accent)` on each text-bearing element inside a dark container. Failure to do this produces invisible dark-on-dark text. 4. **Use flexbox and CSS grid** freely for layout. 5. **Use class names** that describe the layout's purpose (e.g., `.pillar-grid`, `.metric-row`, `.phase-timeline`). Invent clear, semantic names. Every custom class used in the HTML must have a matching rule in the `

TITLE: Diplomacy is failing to stabilize the border despite existing mechanisms
SUBTITLE: Political-security outlook
Assess why de-escalation has not held: the November 2024 ceasefire framework remains incomplete, Israeli and Hezbollah actions continue to test the Blue Line, and Lebanese state institutions remain too weak to fully impose control in the south. End with a concise outlook on escalation risks.

Key facts:
- UNIFIL and the Lebanese Army had resumed joint patrols along the Blue Line after the 2024 war, but deployment remained incomplete where Israeli forces had not fully withdrawn from Lebanese areas.
- UN humanitarian officials launched a Lebanon Flash Appeal for March to May 2026 in response to the renewed escalation, underscoring that the crisis had moved beyond a contained border incident.
- Recent reporting indicates regional diplomacy is linking any Lebanon de-escalation to the wider confrontation involving Israel, Iran, and allied armed groups, increasing the difficulty of a standalone settlement.

Sources:
- UNIFIL update on joint patrols: https://unifil.unmissions.org/unifil-and-lebanese-army-resume-patrolling-together-along-blue-line-0 (Shows partial restoration of security mechanisms and unresolved withdrawal issues.)
- UN Humanitarian Coordinator statement, Mar 2026: https://lebanon.un.org/en/312364-statement-un-humanitarian-coordinator-imran-riza-un-geneva-press-briefing (Confirms renewed escalation and launch of Flash Appeal.)
- Reuters-reported summary via Guardian live blog, 25 Mar 2026: https://www.theguardian.com/world/live/2026/mar/25/middle-east-crisis-live-iran-war-oil-prices-more-us-troops-reportedly-deployed-donald-trump-attacks-on-lebanon?page=with%3Ablock-69c447e18f0875678d6f8272 (Indicates Lebanon is being tied into broader regional ceasefire bargaining.)

[Design Style: BASE VIBE - The solid foundation.
Use standard Strategy& styling:
- Clean left accent bars (4px maroon #8E1E1E)
- White card backgrounds with subtle shadows
- Clear visual hierarchy: title > subtitle > content
- Consistent spacing and typography
- Professional, clean, no embellishments
This is the default, well-tested layout that works reliably.]

Layout: Use a two-column slide: left side 'Why de-escalation failed' with three bullets; right side 'What happens next' with a risk matrix covering limited border war, prolonged southern occupation, and broader regional spillover. Add a footer noting that the outlook is highly contingent on regional diplomacy.

message.content:
Diplomacy is failing to stabilize the border despite existing mechanisms

Political-security outlook

Why de-escalation failed

Incomplete Security Framework -- UNIFIL and Lebanese Army patrols remain limited by ongoing Israeli presence in contested areas, preventing full restoration of state control.

Humanitarian Crisis -- The March 2026 Flash Appeal confirms the conflict has transcended localized border skirmishes, requiring urgent international intervention.

Regional Entanglement -- Lebanon de-escalation is now tethered to broader negotiations between Israel, Iran, and regional proxies, complicating standalone settlements.

What happens next
Limited Border War
Continued tactical exchanges along the Blue Line with high risk of miscalculation.
Prolonged Occupation
Israeli forces maintain buffer zones in southern Lebanon, deepening institutional paralysis.
Regional Spillover
Escalation risks rise as Lebanon becomes a primary theater for wider regional power struggles.
Source: UNIFIL, UN Humanitarian Coordinator, Reuters/Guardian (Mar 2026); Outlook contingent on regional diplomacyPage 1
